5. **Write the report in Markdown**

   - Detailed description of the chosen/best idea, including rationale, pseudocode, and implementation notes

The report must be focused, technically accurate. Being concise with 200-500 words without trivial and redundant information.
Support all claims with evidence and references, and remain tightly aligned with the target problem.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

The supplied code contains the diagnosis module only; HSTU internals and the final sequence readout cannot be verified. Diagnosis reads item embeddings through `view.item_emb.weight`, obtains per-position features through `view.log2feats(sequence)`, and scores candidates through `view.predict_score(features, items)`. It does not explicitly select a final user representation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(view, device)` stores the compatibility view and its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`; the latter two are unused. The actual network is accessed through `view.model` for `itemnum`.

The loader supplies `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` tensors of shape `B × L`. The probe converts sequences to NumPy, computes features, stacks positive and negative IDs into `B × L × 2`, and obtains corresponding logits. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded.

# Probes & Metrics

- **Embedding collapse:** Samples up to 2,048 item embeddings with seed 42, excluding padding and reserved tokens. It normalizes embeddings, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the result to `[0,1]`. Higher values indicate directional alignment; approximately 0.5 corresponds to average cosine zero.
- **Positive–negative separation:** In evaluation mode without gradients, examines up to ten training batches. It reports mean and 10th-percentile positive-minus-negative margins, the fraction below zero, and the fraction below `eps=0.5`. Larger margins and smaller failure fractions suggest stronger sampled-pair separation.
- **Category breakdown:** Counts positive and negative item category occurrences among weak-margin and wrong-rank positions, retaining the top twenty categories per group. These are raw counts, without exposure normalization.

# Perturbation & Tests

No histories are shuffled, masked, or otherwise perturbed. Embedding subsampling and supplied negative candidates are the only sampling mechanisms. The probes assess embedding geometry and training-pair separation, not sequence sensitivity.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`, containing five scalar metrics and a nested category breakdown. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into instructions requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; interpretation occurs separately.

Unavailable category metadata yields empty category lists. The module does not measure validation HR@10, generalization, full-catalog recommendation diversity, temporal sensitivity, or final-position readout correctness. For an equal-user estimand, average paired differences across repeats within each prefix, then prefixes within each user; average user effects within each category. Obtain a 95% percentile interval from the replicate macro means’ 2.5th/97.5th percentiles; do not average category interval endpoints. If identifiable users span categories, resample their complete cross-category records jointly. This applies the principle that resampling must preserve within-subject dependence and reflect sampling design. Without reliable user IDs, user-clustered confidence intervals are unavailable: sequence hashes cannot reliably join overlapping prefixes or distinguish users with identical histories. Defensible reporting is descriptive paired effects, empirical quantiles, observed row/prefix counts, and explicitly conditional variability across perturbation seeds—not population confidence intervals or independent-user sample sizes. Recommended implementation: construct a seeded audit sample from public user histories when available; otherwise label it a row sample. Recommended protocol: for each nonpadding shifted target y=positive[b,t], use only sequence[b,:t+1], including the current item but excluding later positions. The original [SASRec sampler](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/sampler.py) confirms this next-item alignment. Re-pad each prefix on the left and read its final nonpadding position; never use count−1 as an absolute index. Earlier occurrences of y are legitimate history: do not remove them. With one sampled negative, report pairwise accuracy, score margin and tie rate; HR@10 over two candidates is trivially one.

For informative rank diagnostics, predeclare a larger candidate count, such as one target plus 999 unique negatives. Freeze candidates per category/user/target-position using a deterministic seed; sample without replacement, excluding padding, y and prefix-seen items. Never inspect future or held-out interactions to filter diagnostic negatives. Keep y exactly once even when previously seen. For an unseen-only diagnostic, instead mark repeated targets ineligible and report eligibility counts and coverage separately. If the pool is insufficient, use all eligible items and disclose actual candidate counts. These are proposed diagnostic conventions; preserve the host evaluator’s eligibility rules unchanged.

Define deterministic ordering by descending score, then ascending item ID: rank(y)=1+count(scores greater than y)+count(equal scores with smaller item ID). Report ties; placing the target first must not confer priority. Explicit tie policies matter because [ranking conventions differ](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.rankdata.html). Label these results training-prefix sampled diagnostics, with candidate count and aggregation documented. They are neither held-out generalization estimates nor the benchmark’s macro validation HR@10: 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives, seed 42. [Sampled-metric research](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/) shows that candidate sampling can change model comparisons.

HSTU can encode both relative position and elapsed time through attention biases; check which channels the supplied implementation actually uses ([HSTU analysis](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.00714)). Suggested controls: delete equal numbers of recent versus oldest events on the same eligible users; separately delete only the final event, and delete recent events while preserving the final event. Recent deletion including the last item changes both context and the readout item, so greater degradation alone cannot distinguish broad recency reliance from final-item dependence. Shuffle only the preceding history while fixing the final item, sequence length, padding and candidate set. Repeat permutations; measure paired HR@10 changes and prediction/rank stability. Always read the final nonpadding position in left-padded inputs.

Timestamp and position handling define different interventions. For deletion, preserve surviving events’ original timestamps and the prediction-time reference; recompute time differences without compressing elapsed time. Compare normal compacted positions with an explicit original-position-ID control where supported; naive padding holes can change masking. For shuffling, permuting item identities over fixed chronological timestamp slots tests item-to-time/position assignment. Moving item–timestamp pairs together preserves event identity but creates nonchronological input and potentially unusual signed time differences. Report these separately. Within the same trained HSTU, diagnostic position-bias and time-bias ablations can expose sensitivity, but are themselves distribution shifts.

These are proposed identification controls, not established causal conclusions. Temporal counterfactual research emphasizes preserving dependencies and proximity to observed histories ([CETD](https://www.mdpi.com/2076-3417/13/20/11176)). Under unrealistic deletions or shuffles, defensible conclusions concern model sensitivity to the specified perturbation. They do not establish causal user preferences, prove that order is useful in natural histories, or show that robustness implies the model ignores history.
